Thanks for the ping. Quick technical summary and proposal:

- Feasibility: Yes — we can publish artifacts to an S3 bucket per-customer with lifecycle rules and prefix-level encryption. We already support generating pre-signed GET URLs (TTL configurable).
- Access model: We recommend two access modes: (A) GovGate pulls using short-lived pre-signed URLs we publish to a secure webhook (recommended for automation); (B) GovGate assumes a read-only cross-account role with scoped policies (useful for large bulk transfers).
- Audit and retention: We'll emit CloudTrail records and object-level metadata; we can retain download logs for 90 days by default and extend to 365 on request (costs apply).
- SLA: We can commit to artifact publication within 24 hours of request during business hours for standard evidence. For incident-level artifacts (hot logs), propose 4-hour turnaround subject to priority routing.
- Pen-test coordination: We will provide a customer-facing pen-test contact and can accept scan windows. If GovGate wants to bring a third-party pen-test firm, we'll require a signed ToR and an NDA and will coordinate change windows with our infra team.

Estimated dev effort to build the webhook + presigned automation: 2 sprints (4 weeks) with 1 engineer + part-time security SME. If GovGate chooses cross-account role mode, effort reduces to ~1.5 weeks for IAM policy templates and guardrails.

Attachments: govgate_grc_connector_spec.pdf (from GovGate), redwood_sla_template_v2.docx (our template).

Next steps: 1) confirm preferred access mode, 2) sign off on SLA/retention numbers, 3) schedule the pen-test coordination call.

-Vivek
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
